skill.description: Use AgentDB advanced features for QUIC synchronization, hybrid vector search, multi-database coordination, and production operations.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, private example IP addresses, local SQLite paths, and documentation links. The audit confirms one privileged firewall command and adds semantic concerns for unpinned npx execution and broad QUIC port exposure.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the broad sudo firewall example with a warning and source-restricted UDP rules for trusted peers only.
Pin AgentDB CLI versions in examples and advise users to inspect packages before executing remote CLI tools.
Add explicit guidance for peer authentication, private networks, and secure QUIC configuration before production use.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Execution in CLI Examples
semantic_findings.description: Several examples use npx agentdb@latest. Running the latest package can execute changing remote code and makes the command behavior less reproducible.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands repeatedly call npx with @latest in user-facing instructions. This is a clear supply-chain risk, although legitimate CLI documentation may use it for convenience.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad QUIC Firewall Opening
semantic_findings.description: The troubleshooting guidance opens UDP port 4433 without source restrictions or authentication guidance. On a public host, this can expose the synchronization service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited troubleshooting block explicitly permits UDP traffic to the sync port. The surrounding text does not limit the rule to trusted peers.

content.value_statement: Advanced AgentDB setups need clear patterns for sync, search, and operations. This skill gives practical guidance for distributed vector database workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains QUIC synchronization setup, peer configuration, batch sizing, and retry options.
Compares cosine, Euclidean, and dot product distance metrics with common use cases.
Shows hybrid vector search with metadata filters and weighted scoring concepts.
Describes multi-database separation, sharding, MMR, and context synthesis patterns.
Outlines CLI import, export, optimization, and troubleshooting workflows.
Lists environment variables for AgentDB performance and sync configuration.
limitations: It provides documentation examples only and does not run AgentDB commands by itself.
It assumes Node.js, agentic-flow, and vector search knowledge.
Security guidance for exposed QUIC peers needs additional production review.
Commands must be adapted and verified before use in real systems.

use_cases.title: Plan QUIC-Synchronized AgentDB Nodes
use_cases.description: Design peer settings, ports, retries, and sync intervals for a multi-node AgentDB deployment.

use_cases.title: Design Hybrid Vector Search
use_cases.description: Combine semantic similarity with metadata filters, weighted scoring, and result diversification.

use_cases.title: Operate Multiple AgentDB Stores
use_cases.description: Separate knowledge, conversations, and code data while planning sharding and maintenance workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Distance Metrics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner comparison for search quality decisions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain when I should use cosine, Euclidean, or dot product search in AgentDB. Keep the answer practical.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Hybrid Search Filters
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design an AgentDB hybrid search strategy for documents with category, recency, and citation metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Design QUIC Sync Topology
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for distributed AgentDB nodes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a secure AgentDB QUIC sync plan for three trusted nodes. Include ports, peer rules, retries, and monitoring checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AgentDB production plan for sharding, backups, optimization, sync safety, and troubleshooting gaps.

output_examples.input: Compare cosine and Euclidean search for text embeddings.
output_examples.output: Cosine is recommended for normalized text embeddings and semantic similarity. Euclidean is better when vector magnitude or spatial distance matters.

output_examples.input: Plan a three-node AgentDB sync setup.
output_examples.output: A suitable plan includes trusted peer addresses, one UDP sync port, retry limits, batch sizes, monitoring checks, and restricted firewall rules.

output_examples.input: Improve hybrid search results for research papers.
output_examples.output: Use semantic retrieval first, then apply filters for year, category, and citation thresholds. Add MMR when results become repetitive.

best_practices: Use private networks or authenticated peer access for QUIC synchronization.
Pin CLI package versions and verify commands before execution.
Separate unrelated memory domains into different databases or shards.
anti_patterns: Opening synchronization ports broadly on public interfaces.
Copying example IP addresses or latest package commands without review.
Mixing unrelated knowledge, conversation, and code data in one store.

faq.question: Does this skill run AgentDB commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and guidance that a user or agent can adapt.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it cover QUIC synchronization?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains peer configuration, ports, intervals, retries, and troubleshooting concepts.

faq.question: Can it choose a vector distance metric?
faq.answer: It explains tradeoffs so you can choose based on data type and retrieval goals.

faq.question: Is the guidance enough for production security?
faq.answer: No. Production use needs additional review for authentication, network exposure, and package execution.

faq.question: How should I handle the firewall example?
faq.answer: Treat it as risky. Restrict source peers and review network policy before changing firewall rules.
